metadata.title: viz ingest pipeline
metadata.intent: Self-monitoring for viz operators. Answers: is telemetry being accepted, acknowledged and made durable on time, and if not, which stage (edge, shard, flush to object storage, ledger) is behind?

cell.label: Cell
cell.description: Deployment cell; a cell owns a pool of shards.

server_errors.title: Ingest 5xx ratio
server_errors.description: Share of ingest requests answered with 5xx. Clients retry these, so a short spike is tolerable; above 1% data is at risk of being dropped by client buffers.

reject_share.title: Rejected samples
reject_share.description: Share of samples refused (limits, validation, out-of-order). Rejections are deliberate, but a jump means a tenant hit a limit or a client is misbehaving.

durability_window.title: Oldest unflushed data
durability_window.description: Age of the oldest acknowledged data not yet in object storage, worst shard. This is the durability exposure; it should stay under the flush interval.

accepted_rate.title: Accepted samples by signal
accepted_rate.description: Samples, spans and log lines accepted per second. A drop with no rise in rejections means senders stopped or the edge is unreachable.

rejections.title: Rejected samples by reason
rejections.description: Refused samples per second by reason. rate_limited and series_limit are tenant limits; invalid and out_of_order point at a client bug.

ack_latency_by_cell.title: Acknowledgement latency by cell
ack_latency_by_cell.description: Time from request arrival to acknowledgement at the selected quantile, per cell. One cell above the others means a hot or unhealthy shard pool.

ack_distribution.title: Acknowledgement latency distribution
ack_distribution.description: Histogram of acknowledgement time. A second band forming near the client timeout means requests are queueing behind a slow shard.

unflushed_by_cell.title: Oldest unflushed data by cell
unflushed_by_cell.description: Durability exposure per cell. A sawtooth under the flush interval is healthy; a ramp means flushes are failing or slow.

flush_time.title: Flush duration
flush_time.description: Time to seal a batch and write it to object storage, at the selected quantile. Rising flush time with flat volume points at object storage.

flush_errors.title: Flush failures by stage
flush_errors.description: Failed flush attempts per second by stage (seal, put, record). Should be zero; failures are retried but each one widens the durability window.

flushed_volume.title: Bytes written to object storage
flushed_volume.description: Compressed bytes flushed per second by signal. Use with accepted samples to watch the compression ratio and storage cost.

ledger_commit_lag.title: Ledger commit lag
ledger_commit_lag.description: Delay between a file landing in object storage and its record being committed to the ledger. Until committed, the data is durable but not queryable.

compaction.title: Compaction backlog
compaction.description: Small files waiting to be compacted, per cell. A growing backlog does not lose data but makes queries slower and more expensive.

shards.title: Shards under pressure
shards.description: Per shard: buffer fill, active series and p99 acknowledgement time, fullest first. A shard near 1.0 buffer fill will start rejecting writes.

error_logs.title: Error log lines by component
error_logs.description: Error-level log lines per step from the ingest, shard and ledger components. Use it to see which component started complaining first.
